findings.issue: For standalone clarity, specify that pKa for the weak-base half-equivalence case belongs to HB⁺, as the SCORE steps already correctly state. This is correct derived chemistry, not an error.
findings.evidence: Applying Henderson–Hasselbalch to HB⁺/B gives pH = pKa(HB⁺) + log([B]/[HB⁺]). At equal concentrations, pH = pKa(HB⁺).
